name: Bisabolol
description: Bisabolol (CAS 515-69-5 ), also known as α-Bisabolol, is a naturally derived monocyclic sesquiterpene alcohol originally sourced from German chamomile. It is now predominantly produced synthetically or from candeia tree oil for industrial use. It functions as a skin-conditioning agent and active carrier in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations. This ingredient is highly valued for its ability to enhance the penetration of other actives into the skin layers. In skincare formulations, it is used as a primary soothing and moisturizing agent in creams, serums, and lotions. These products typically target sensitive or reactive skin types requiring gentle care. Its carrier properties make it a preferred solvent for active ingredients in topical pharmaceutical preparations. This includes wound-care products and medicated creams where high purity and efficacy are essential. Fragrance formulators incorporate it as a fixative and mild floral base note in fine fragrances and functional perfumery. It also appears in after-sun products, baby care lines, and anti-aging formulations. The material is supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid. Standard commercial grades include natural and synthetic variants, with natural-origin material often certified to differentiate supply chains. Cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are both available to meet industry needs.
